name: Temporary Residence Permit -- Investment

requirements.blocker_text: EUR 50,000+ share-capital investment in a Latvian company with fewer than 50 employees, or EUR 100,000+ in a larger company, plus a EUR 10,000 state budget fee.
requirements.fix_path: Contribute the required minimum share capital to a qualifying Latvian company and pay the state budget fee.

requirement_groups.name: State-managed alternative investment fund (new route, June 2026)

requirements.blocker_text: EUR 150,000+ investment in a state-created alternative investment fund, held for at least 5 years and confirmed as actively invested by the fund manager, plus a EUR 10,000 state budget payment.
requirements.fix_path: Invest at least EUR 150,000 in the designated state-managed alternative investment fund and pay the state budget fee.

evidence_required.document: Proof of share-capital contribution or fund investment
Proof of the EUR 10,000 state budget payment
Tax-compliance evidence for the underlying company (corporate track)

outcome.duration_length: corporate investment: 2 years (reduced from 5 years); alternative fund: 5 years

sources.title: Cobalt (regional law firm) -- Latvia's New Immigration Law (effective 11 June 2026): real estate and subordinated-bond routes eliminated; new EUR 150,000 state-fund route created; corporate investment (EUR 50,000/100,000) retained but duration cut from 5 to 2 years; both tracks carry a EUR 10,000 state budget fee
LV Portals (Latvijas Vestnesis) -- corroborates the same June 2026 changes: real estate/bond elimination, new EUR 150,000 fund route, corporate investment duration cut to 2 years

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Latvia). STATUS: DRAFT -- corroborated by two independent sources describing the same 11 June 2026 law, but neither is a directly-fetched PMLP or likumi.lv page for the amended Immigration Law text itself. FLAGGED PROMINENTLY: Latvia's REAL ESTATE (EUR 250,000+) and BANK SUBORDINATED-BOND (EUR 280,000+) investment residence routes -- long the country's best-known 'golden visa' pathways, and still described as currently active by at least one tier-3 blog fetched in this same research pass (immigrantinvest.com) and even by PMLP's OWN English-language duration page (https://www.pmlp.gov.lv/en/how-long-may-residence-permit-be-issued, fetched directly in this pass) -- were ELIMINATED by this new law as of 11 June 2026, less than 3 months before this build. This is a textbook stale-source trap: multiple sources that read as current (including Latvia's own official PMLP page) describe a program that no longer exists for new applicants. Existing real-estate/bond permit holders may renew once under transition rules but the routes are closed to new entrants -- not modeled as an ongoing 'route' here since it is not available to a new applicant, consistent with this dataset's convention of documenting what is actually obtainable now rather than what a stale source still describes.
